lines.text: The name is said to point to lapis imported from Asia.
The finest lapis came from Badakhshan, in northeastern Afghanistan.
lines.say: The finest lapis came from bah-dahk-SHAHN, in northeastern Afghanistan.

lines.text: Grinding lapis alone gives only a dull grayish blue.
A resin and wax dough washed the blue out of the powder.
The first washes gave the best blue, and later ones were grayer.
Some sources say it sometimes cost more than gold.
Painters used it sparingly, often for the robes of the Virgin.
In 1824 a French society offered a prize for a synthetic version.

post.caption: Ultramarine means beyond the sea. The name is said to point to lapis imported from Asia. The finest lapis came from Badakhshan, in northeastern Afghanistan. Grinding lapis alone gives only a dull grayish blue. A resin and wax dough washed the blue out of the powder. The first washes gave the best blue, and later ones were grayer. Some sources say it sometimes cost more than gold. Painters used it sparingly, often for the robes of the Virgin. In 1824 a French society offered a prize for a synthetic version. Guimet won the prize in 1828 with a recipe from 1826.
